research.note: RESEARCH.md on ispc-dev: leader techniques, literature, ISPC techniques, ranked ideas. Sandbox Xeon numbers only; nothing run on Zen by the agent.

ideas.title: Vector dense kernel (lane-constant ORs)
ideas.summary: Per-lane single-bit ORs that LLVM folds into constant vector ORs, as SLP does for Rust. Same idea as hc-002.

ideas.title: No masked tails on AVX2
ideas.summary: ~2,000 vmaskmovpd stores a pass; pad planes to 16 words and overrun unmasked (OR is idempotent).

ideas.title: One-member fast path for 13
ideas.summary: 13 alone costs ~9k cycles a pass because apply_group streams seven empty patterns.

ideas.title: Raise dense limit to 192-256
ideas.summary: Vector dense costs a flat ~2k cycles per factor; sparse 131-251 costs more.

ideas.title: Start-up autotune of thresholds
ideas.summary: Time a few settings before the timed loop, as C5 does; insurance for untested runners.

ideas.title: Cut lead-in overhead
ideas.summary: Start all group members at the earliest start word, clear own bits after.

ideas.title: Arithmetic masks for some members
ideas.summary: Balance load and ALU ports for primes above 64.

other_lane.assessment: Other permits nothing the wheel cannot already use, and the faithful 1-bit board ranks all algorithms together; our wheel already beats rogiervandam C at 1T on Zen 3-5. Tying his C from the odds-only prototype needs about +19%: 3-5 days, about a one-in-three chance on Zen 5.
other_lane.recommendation: Do not build solution_3 now. Revisit after the PR merges; if a reviewer retags the wheel as other, it already wins that lane.
